title: Editorial: Artificial intelligence requires human intelligence
content: From Google AI (8 August 2026): “President Trump’s science advisor and Office of Science and Technology Policy Director, Michael Kratsios, has strongly advocated for artificial intelligence, spearheading a major policy shift to redirect billions in federal research funding away from universities and toward AI and tech enterprise.” AI did not issue or craft Mr. Kratsios’s policy shift but provides a summary of his actions. The important point is that AI does not generate de novo data, but relies on humans to collect, analyze, and interpret the data, as with this summary of Mr. Kratsios’s actions. Similarly, using AI to address the questions, what is the evidence that human burning of fossil fuels is causing climate change, AI generates the following answer (AI, 8 August 2026, bold is reflected in AI’s answer): “The evidence that human consumption of fossil fuels is causing climate change is overwhelming and clear, established through multiple independent lines of scientific evidence.” AI further summarizes the evidence (paraphrased): “1. Smoking gun chemical fingerprint (isotope ratios, shift in atmospheric levels of CO2, microscopic decline in oxygen), 2. Basic physics, the greenhouse effect (heat-trapping gases, satellite proof of less heat escaping the atmosphere, ground instruments indicate an increase in infrared radiation returning to the Earth’s surface), 3. Unprecedented coincidence of timing (increase of CO2 in the atmosphere correlates with temperature rise and human consumption of fossil fuels), 4. Climate models exclude natural factors (such as solar activity, volcanoes, and changes in the Earth’s orbit), 5. Fingerprints within the atmosphere point directly to greenhouse effects of CO2 emission rather than processes related to the sun (layer cooling, i.e., the upper atmosphere is actually cooling because greenhouse gases keep heat from reaching the upper atmosphere, but the Sun’s activity would uniformly heat both layers, night temperatures are increasing at a faster rate than daytime temperatures congruent with greenhouse gases trapping heat through the 24-hour cycle while solar variation would mostly affect daytime heat).” AI also provides more evidence, including how increasing CO2 emissions correlate with acidification of the oceans, and so on. The point we wish to make is that the overwhelming and clear evidence that climate warming is due to the burning of fossil fuels is based on the scientific endeavor reflecting the work of scientists across generations (at least as long ago as Eunice Foote’s paper “Circumstances Affecting the Heat of the Sun’s Rays” (1856), American Journal of Science and Arts, where she demonstrated the consequences of the CO2’s heat-retention properties). Shifting resources away from scientific activities (funding research, training of new cadres of scientists, recruitment of the best and brightest, etc.) will only impede our collective efforts to address the existential challenges facing humanity, including climate change and biodiversity loss and redistribution. AI is a valuable tool, but it can only be as valuable as the human research and insight that underpin it. It is also bad business. Where do you think, Mr. Kratsios, does industry recruit scientists—certainly not from the Ethernet?
